message.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Debugging is a critical but challenging task for programmers. This paper proposes
                    <jats:sc>ChatDBG,</jats:sc>
                    an AI-powered debugging assistant.
                    <jats:sc>ChatDBG</jats:sc>
                    integrates large language models (LLMs) to significantly enhance the capabilities and user-friendliness of conventional debuggers.
                    <jats:sc>ChatDBG</jats:sc>
                    lets programmers engage in a collaborative dialogue with the debugger, allowing them to pose complex questions about program state, perform root cause analysis for crashes or assertion failures, and explore open-ended queries like ‘
                    <jats:monospace>why is x null?</jats:monospace>
                    ’. To handle these queries,
                    <jats:sc>ChatDBG</jats:sc>
                    grants the LLM autonomy to
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">take the wheel:</jats:italic>
                    it can act as an independent agent capable of querying and controlling the debugger to navigate through stacks and inspect program state. It then reports its findings and yields back control to the programmer. By leveraging the real-world knowledge embedded in LLMs,
                    <jats:sc>ChatDBG</jats:sc>
                    can diagnose issues identifiable only through the use of domain-specific reasoning. Our
                    <jats:sc>ChatDBG</jats:sc>
                    prototype integrates with standard debuggers including LLDB and GDB for native code and Pdb for Python. Our evaluation across a diverse set of code, including C/C++ code with known bugs and a suite of Python code including standalone scripts and Jupyter notebooks, demonstrates that
                    <jats:sc>ChatDBG</jats:sc>
                    can successfully analyze root causes, explain bugs, and generate accurate fixes for a wide range of real-world errors. For the Python programs, a single query led to an actionable bug fix 67% of the time; one additional follow-up query increased the success rate to 85%.
                    <jats:sc>ChatDBG</jats:sc>
                    has seen rapid uptake; it has already been downloaded more than 75,000 times.
                  </jats:p>
title: ChatDBG: Augmenting Debugging with Large Language Models
